final_text: I fixed the bug in `Gameplay.fs`, and the ball now bounces off the paddle, walls and bricks. The ball's starting velocity was set with `Entity.LinearVelocity @= ...`, and in Nu's ImSim `@=` re-applies a property every frame. Because the value includes `Gen.randomf`, the game picked a new random downward velocity each frame. That wiped out every bounce (so the ball went straight through the paddle) and changed its direction slightly each frame, which caused the wobble. I changed it to `.=`, which sets the velocity only once when the ball is created. I reloaded the code in the live editor and checked it with no keyboard input. The ball bounced upward off the paddle at about Y = -149, then stayed between the walls for the next 400 frames and broke a brick (score 100).

I fixed it with a one-line change in `Gameplay.fs`, line 124. The ball's starting velocity was declared with `Entity.LinearVelocity @= ...`, which re-applies the value every frame, and the value includes a new `Gen.randomf` each time. So every frame the physics bounce was thrown away and the ball got a fresh, slightly different downward velocity. That's why it went through the paddle and wobbled. I changed `@=` to `.=`, so the velocity is set only once when the ball is created and the collision code's bounces are kept. I reloaded the code in the live editor and ran the game screen with no keyboard input for about 1,000 frames. The ball bounced (it was moving upward again), broke bricks (score went to 200) and kept its normal speed of 150. With no one moving the paddle it also lost a life, which is expected.
